summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with HCV- and alcohol-related cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma, and type 2 diabetes was admitted for abdominal pain and hepatic encephalopathy. She presented with confusion and asterixis, linked to noncompliance with lactulose. Treatment with lactulose, Miralax, and senna resolved her encephalopathy. Abdominal imaging revealed new, enlarged lymph nodes concerning for HCC metastasis, prompting an EUS with FNA and fiducial placement. Her pain was managed with oxycodone and gabapentin. Diabetes was stabilized with simplified insulin therapy. She was discharged home with plans to follow up with her hepatologist for biopsy results and possible oncology referral, with emphasis on medication adherence to prevent future encephalopathy episodes.
